They provide a supportive surface that cushions the body during various postures, ensuring both grip and a clean barrier between the practitioner and the floor.

Customization Options

High-Quality Materials

Reliable Manufacturing Expertise

Choosing the Right Yoga Mat Material # Selecting a yoga mat involves considering material properties alongside personal preferences and practice requirements. Here are some common materials and their characteristics:
1. PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride) # Closed-cell surface for durability and superior grip, even in wet conditions Affordable and long-lasting, ideal for studios and budget-conscious users May emit a chemical odor, which some users may find noticeable 2. TPE (Thermoplastic Elastomer) # Eco-friendly and recyclable Good grip and cushioning Less durable than PVC, with potential for earlier wear 3. PU (Polyurethane) # Excellent dry grip and moisture absorption, suitable for hot yoga Moderate durability, requires regular cleaning Lower scratch resistance compared to PVC 4. Natural Rubber # Sustainable and provides ample joint cushioning Absorbs sweat and offers excellent grip in sweaty conditions Sensitive to sunlight, can deform in high temperatures, and less portable 5. POE (Polyolefin Elastomer) # Durable with excellent cushioning and non-slip surface Lightweight and portable Like natural rubber, should be protected from prolonged direct sunlight For bulk orders, Elysian serves as a comprehensive yoga mat factory, offering a wide range of affordable mats to suit various preferences.
